messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Travis for continuous integration?
parts:
One of the best software developers I know just recommended
Travis, a free continuous integration server for open-source
projects:

https://travis-ci.org/

I don't know anything about it, but trust my friend's taste
and like the price.

- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Travis for continuous integration?
parts:
Yeah, it was actually one of my reasons for moving to GitHub back in the day.

At that point, I think there were a couple reasons why I didn't follow through:
- tool chain for C++ -- I think whatever thoughts I had on that have been resolved
- maximum time -- it used to be capped at 20 minutes per build, which we were pushing and definitely not hitting using g++ without the parallel flag.
- RAM -- I thought that was an issue.

It looks like it's come a long way since the last time I looked at it. Let's get it set up.


Daniel

P.S. By "let's," I really mean I'm volunteering, but anyone else can take a stab at it. It's just on a queue below a couple bigger items.
